reason: The narrative demonstrates collaboration between Jacob (family patriarch/leader) and his sons (the people). Jacob sends his sons to Egypt with his authority and instruction. The brothers work collectively in their dealings with Joseph, support one another during their crisis, and speak through Judah as their representative when appealing to Joseph. Judah specifically persuades Jacob to release Benjamin by taking personal responsibility, showing the leader and people working toward mutual survival and family reunion. Their coordinated efforts to obtain grain, return to Egypt, and ultimately relocate to Egypt demonstrate sustained collaboration, even if motivated by necessity (famine) rather than purely voluntary partnership. Pharaoh, Joseph, and the family also coordinate to settle them in Goshen.
